method: AI-assisted source review of a purposive sample with one app per assignment category. Two decision-critical checks per app. A separate reviewer has not signed off.
checks: Developer Edition is a development path. Commercial edition and API entitlement determine production access.
The vendor labels Headless 360 beta. Its initial operations concentrate on administration.
Intercom explicitly places the private access-token path in a paid workspace. The draft left the paid requirement open.
Public integrations that access other workspaces must use OAuth.
The provider has a remote OAuth server. Its install follows standard Slack app approval and a free developer sandbox is available for testing.
The documented Slack server can search workspace information and perform Slack actions within authorized access.
The current onboarding flow uses OAuth and project access levels. Older developer-token pages can conflict with the sunset notice.
Test access is available on enabling the API. A Cloud project needs production access before calling a production account.
Orders, Inventory and Transactions are documented for Core, Plus, Advanced and legacy Commerce Advanced. Plan generation and endpoint matter.
Squarespace documents a remote MCP with catalog, contacts and order tools.
The web MCP has a recurring free quota. Product-level API pricing needs its own review.
The maintainer documents 5,000 monthly free requests, shared by team accounts.
Sentry documents Bearer tokens and OAuth 2.0 authorization code.
The token tutorial names Manager or Admin for its organization-level token flow. The draft mentioned only project membership and scopes.
Jira Cloud scripts use account email plus API token in HTTP Basic. Distributed apps can use OAuth authorization code (3LO).
Atlassian documents OAuth 2.1 as primary and organization-controlled token support.
Stripe test keys use an isolated environment. Activating the account is required before accepting live payments.
The MCP guide documents OAuth and an agent API key fallback, separately from credentials for the REST API.
Devin publishes a hosted server in addition to the client for third-party MCP servers.
The v3 permissions guide documents enterprise service users and role-based permissions.

12.detail: Private access tokens require a paid Intercom workspace. Public apps use OAuth. Confirm the target plan and region for rollout.

21.detail: The remote Slack MCP uses OAuth. Workspace app-approval policies can require admin installation. Developers can try it in Slack’s free sandbox.

31.detail: Use the vendor’s Google Cloud project route. Its documented local Google Ads MCP inherits the API access tier.

46.detail: For Orders, Inventory and Transactions, the help article lists Core, Plus, Advanced and legacy Commerce Advanced. Check the operation and site plan before requesting the site key.

57.detail: Bright Data’s web MCP documents 5,000 free monthly requests, shared per team. Product-specific REST and proxy quotas differ.

70.detail: REST supports OAuth authorization code and Bearer tokens. The organization-token guide requires a Manager or Admin. Prefer a scope limited to the first operation.

74.detail: REST uses OAuth 2.0 3LO or email and API token in HTTP Basic. The Rovo MCP uses OAuth 2.1 and supports tokens when the organization permits the flow.

81.detail: Use isolated test keys before live account activation. Stripe MCP separately supports OAuth or a designated agent API key.

96.detail: The hosted Devin MCP at https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp uses a Bearer key. Devin can also consume external MCP servers. Enterprise REST permissions depend on the service-user role.

50.detail: Indexed vendor documentation describes a seller-portal API key used to obtain an environment-specific checkout session secret. Confirm API entitlement and sandbox or production key provisioning with FanBasis.
